title: Kargil Martyr's Family Still Waiting for Promises Made 26 Years Ago
summary: The family of a Kargil martyr, who died in 1999, is still awaiting promises made 26 years ago. The martyr's son, Vijay Kumar, was killed in action during the Kargil conflict. His family has been demanding compensation and recognition for his sacrifice. In 2015, the Indian government had promised to provide a pension to the families of martyrs, but so far, no payment has been made. The family is now seeking answers from the government on when they will receive their due.
summary_points: Vijay Kumar was killed in action during the Kargil conflict in 1999.
title_hi: कारगिल शहीद के परिवार को 26 साल बाद वादे पूरे नहीं हुए
summary_hi: कारगिल शहीद के परिवार को 26 साल बाद वादे पूरे नहीं हुए। कारगिल में हुए युद्ध में शहीद होने वाले विजय कुमार का परिवार अभी भी अपने बलिदान के लिए वादे 26 साल बाद पूरे नहीं हो रहे हैं।
summary_points_hi: विजय कुमार कारगिल में हुए युद्ध में शहीद होने वाले थे।

framing.center: Centrist coverage largely reported the events without a distinct frame. However, The New Indian Express noted that the family is now seeking answers from the government on when they will receive their due compensation and recognition.
framing.right: Right-leaning outlets framed the funding row as a national-security concern, stressing the foreign-donation angle and the demand for an audit. They highlighted the government's failure to fulfill its promise of providing a pension to the families of martyrs in 2015.

framing_hi.right: विदेशी दान के मुद्दे और एक ऑडिट की मांग पर केंद्रीय सरकार की निष्ठा को उजागर करने वाला राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा चिंता
